content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: move 2 cross-skilled agents to payments 15:00-16:00 and run IVR callback on both queues 19:00-19:45, at no extra cost, for a predicted 88.3% service level against the 80% target.","why":"The gap is a dengue-related sick wave, not extra demand. 11 sick absences are logged on each queue, and payments call volume is 8.7% below forecast. Even with no action, the disruption window (14:30-20:00) is predicted at 87.4%, already above target. P1 is the cheapest plan that follows policy and reaches the target. It lifts payments to 87.8% and general to 89.0%, and trims abandons from 3.4% to 3.2%, at zero cost. Moving 2 agents out of general for one hour still leaves general at 89.0%, so the other queue is not put at risk.","trade_offs":["P0 (no action) also meets target at 87.4% and costs nothing, but P1 adds about a point of service level and lowers abandons for free.","P2 reaches 89.8% (abandon 2.7%) for INR 336, but pushes some customers to chat, which is a modest customer-experience change.","P3 reaches 90.2% (abandon 2.5%) for INR 1,080, and depends on 13 agents accepting overtime.","P4 gives the strongest result at 93.2% (abandon 1.7%) for INR 1,776, which is extra spend the 80% target does not require."],"watch":"Watch payments, which has the thinnest margin at 87.8%, and check for further sick calls before the evening. If more agents drop out and payments heads toward 80%, be ready to switch to P3 overtime for 19:00-20:00. No escalation to the duty manager is needed."}
